What's New

  • Silcrate runs on container 1.3.0. It's the version Silcrate checks for during setup and the one it installs for you — if you're still on 1.2.2, setup will prompt you to update. Nothing you've already created changes: containers, images, volumes and networks carry over untouched.
  • Setup catches a guest kernel left behind by an earlier release. Silcrate used to check only whether some kernel was installed, so a Mac that had one from a previous release kept booting containers on it without ever saying so. The kernel step now compares what's installed against the kernel this release recommends and offers to update it, naming both the release you have and the one you're moving to. The kernel it replaces stays on disk — container has no way to remove it — so you can delete it yourself from ~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.container/kernels if you want the space back.
  • Tracing and profiling work inside containers. The guest kernel that ships with 1.3.0 has eBPF, kprobes, uprobes, ftrace and BTF turned on, so tools that need them run in a container instead of failing against a kernel built without them.

Changes

  • Registry connections are HTTPS unless you say otherwise. The create form's pull-scheme picker no longer offers auto, which container 1.3.0 removed — it used to quietly fall back to plain HTTP for localhost, private-network addresses and names under your local DNS domain. If you pull from a registry that only speaks HTTP, choose http in the create form.

What's New

  • Silcrate runs on container 1.2.2. It's the version Silcrate checks for during setup and the one it installs for you — if you're still on 1.2.0, setup will prompt you to update. Nothing you've already created changes: containers, images, volumes and networks carry over untouched.
  • Containers hit memory limits less often. The 1.2.2 runtime gives each container's virtual machine more headroom for memory mappings, so workloads that map a lot of files — databases, search indexes, big test suites — stop failing on a machine that has memory to spare.

Fixes

  • The update prompt no longer interrupts launch. Silcrate now waits until the app has finished opening before checking for a new version, so the update alert appears over the app itself instead of the splash screen.
